history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the onefivenine Hindu-temples directory for Lamka (Churachandpur) lists this as 'Durga Temple, Saiton, Manipur 795133' - 14.8 km from central Lamka - so 'Churachandpur' in the CSV is the district/town approximation, and the actual locality is Saiton (verify which Saiton locality - onefivenine lists only the name and PIN). Beyond this single directory listing, no web source documents this temple: no photos, founding date, deity forms, festivals or management details could be found. The Saikot-directory view of the same site repeats the identical Saiton entry. A onefivenine-listed 'Nganukon Durga Mandir' in Bishnupur district (~9 km from Churachandpur) is a different shrine and should not be conflated with it. The temple presumably serves the small Hindu/Meitei community of the district. Coordinates below are Churachandpur-town approximate (the Saiton exact point could not be geocoded) - verify on the ground before use. No reliable image found (media empty).

name: Durga Temple
town: Saiton (CSV 'Churachandpur' is approximate - onefivenine lists the temple at Saiton, ~15 km from Lamka)
town_description: Churachandpur (locally called Lamka) is the second-largest town of Manipur and the headquarters of Churachandpur district, about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road. It is the heartland of the Kuki-Chin hill tribes (Thadou-Kuki, Hmar, Paite, Zou) and is overwhelmingly Christian; a small Hindu/Meitei community maintains a handful of shrines in and around the district, including this Durga temple at Saiton.

travel.airport: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport (Imphal, IMF) - about 60 km northeast of Churachandpur (verify).
travel.railway: No rail link to Churachandpur; nearest railhead is Dimapur (Nagaland) or Jiribam (verify).
travel.road: Churachandpur is about 60 km southwest of Imphal on Tiddim Road (NH-102B), connected by buses and shared sumos (verify schedules). Saiton is listed as ~15 km from central Lamka (verify the route locally).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navratri/Durga Puja (Sep-Oct) is the major festival at Durga temples.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Unpublished (verify - visit in the morning or evening when Hindu shrines in the district are typically open; confirm locally).
